Discuss — Example Question (annotated answer with though process)

Sample Answer

Question Breakdown & Tips and Tricks

Question: Discuss the suitability of the Agile development methodology for the start-up company. (4 marks)

Step 1. Read the Question Carefully.

When reading a question, it's important to ask these two questions:

  1. What is the topic/content area? This question is testing your knowledge of the Agile development methodology. This is under the "Research and use the Agile software development approach" dot point of your software engineering project topic. Revise 4.5 Agile Approach, if required.
  2. What are we required to do? Highlight the NESA key verb in red so you don't forget it. We are required to discuss the suitability of the Agile development methodology for that start up company in the stimulus. So, we need to read the stimulus, and then describe the positive and negative aspects of using Agile to develop the software they are making.

 Stimulus: A start-up company is developing a medical record-keeping application for small healthcare providers.

The app needs to comply with strict regulations and must function correctly upon its first release to avoid potential legal and ethical issues.

However, the company has limited resources and requires the project to be developed cost-effectively and with the ability to adapt to feedback from early users.

Step 2. Analyse the stimulus.

Here, the stimulus provides information that reveals how Agile can suit some of their needs, but is not quite the right fit for others. E.g "strict regulation" and "correct upon it's first release" is normally a sign that the waterfall approach should be used, however, "limited resources" and "adapt to feedback" is more Agile's strength. There is a lot here to write about in our response and we must reference the stimulus to get full marks.

Step 3. Plan your response quickly in your head.

In your head take a mental note of the two things you are required to do which is describing the positives and negatives of using Agile to develop this medial software.

  • The positives are that agile will cost less, and be more adaptable to feedback from early users.
  • The negatives are the fact that there are strict regulations and a requirement for the app to be correct and polish when it is released. This is more a strength of the waterfall approach.

Step 4. Write your response

  • Use the correct structure: Make sure you follow the discuss structure. This involves providing positives and negatives.
    • Start with a topic sentence which includes the phrase "many positives and negatives" which signposts to the marker you are going to write a response in the correct format and tells them exactly what is in your question so they can give you marks with minimal friction.
    • Use text connectives between your points. When transitioning between positives and negatives, you can use a word such as "conversely" and "however", to signpost to the marker that you are beginning the next section of your response. Between points of the same side, you can use connectives like "additionally" and "furthermore" to indicate the separation of your points, making it easy for the marker to give you marks.
  • Relate to the Scenario/Question. Never forget the golden rule "relate to the scenario/question". This means you should use terms from the question throughout your response make links back to the ideas/context given in the question. Below, the links back to the question have been highlighted in purple. 
  • Give clear examples. Give examples for extra clarity and to show a detailed, nuanced understanding of a concept. You can also use examples to relate back to the scenario. Below, examples are highlighted in blue. 
  • Know your content. It's important to think about where this question comes from in your syllabus as you read the question, recall what you have learned about that topic and then include as much relevant information as you can to flesh out your answer.

Sample Answer Analysis: There are many positive and negative aspects of using the Agile development methodology for this medical record application. The positives include the cost-effectiveness of Agile, which aligns with the limited resources and budget of the start-up company. This will allow the team to implement core features, such as patient tracking, first, followed by smaller features as updates when revenue is generated. Another benefit is the flexibility of Agile's Scrum/Sprint system, which allows development to mould itself to new requirements and feedback from early users. However, the use of Agile also has some negatives regarding the robust requirements of the first release and the potential legal and ethical repercussions of faulty software. The waterfall method may be more suitable than Agile in this respect, especially when patient health is at stake.

Step 5. Check your response is correct

Quickly reread the question and try highlighting your response in your head if you're in an exam or in a word processor if you are practicing. Make sure there is enough purple and blue and also some green and yellow.

  1. We have structured our response appropriately for a discuss question. Here we have described positive and negatives aspects of Agile in the scenario.
  2. We've related to the scenario. We've also included terms from the question and idea from the stimulus that enhance the nuance and accuracy of our descriptions of each point while simultaneously relating more rigorously to the scenario.

Marking Criteria (through the eyes of a marker)

How do I get full marks?

  • Relate to the scenario and give examples. In the marking criteria, to get full marks, you must discuss both the positive and negative impacts of using Agile. More specifically, you need to do it in relation to the scenario. In this question, the relation to the scenario/examples is worth one mark since without it, you can get a maximum of 3 marks.
  • Structure your response appropriately. A discuss question requires positives and negatives. You need to make sure you clearly describe the positive and negative aspects of the subject you are discussing. Including a topic sentence which addresses the question and tells the marker you are going to address positive and negatives is also important.
  • Know your content — You need to be on top of your data security content. Revise 4.5 Agile Approach

I'm completely stuck. How do I maximise my marks?

  • Don't leave the question blank. If you're totally stuck, there are always some basic things you can do to guarantee at least one or two marks. After this, flag the question so you can come back to it after you finish the rest of the exam, hopefully with fresh ideas to claim a few more marks.
  • In this question, providing some relevant information will get you one mark. This could be as simple as listing some benefits or disadvantages of Agile. If you are able to outline the positive or negative aspect of Agile, you will get two marks, and if you described enough positives and just forgot to include negatives, you could still get three marks if your positives are really good. 
  • Try and put yourself in the shoes of the scenario. Imagine you are the IT team of the software start-up company and using your common sense and understanding of the content, think about the positive and negative impacts of using Agile.

Explain

Explain Questions

NESA Definition — Explain

  • Relate cause and effect.
  • Make the relationships between things evident.
  • Provide why and/or how.

The explain definition from NESA requires us to relate cause and effect. By relating cause and effect, we are able to make the relationship between things evident and provide how something works or why it works.

WHY/HOW Questions

You may also find that some questions in the HSC don't use a specific NESA key verb, but rather use "Why" or "How". When you see these words, you can basically treat them loosely as an "Explain" question. A why question will require you to come up with reasons explaining/linking to a specific outcome and how requires you to relate how components of something work together/what makes something work.

 

Answer Structure

  1. Brief topic sentence or phrase that addresses the question.
  2. Include one or a series of causes which lead to the effect you are trying to explain. You are aiming to take a complex idea an split it into it's atomic components and map out how each piece relates and contributes to the effect you are explaining.

Question Breakdown & Tips and Tricks

Question: Explain two strategies used by software developers to manage the security of programming code. (4 marks)

Step 1. Read the Question Carefully.

When reading a question, it's important to ask these two questions:

  1. What is the topic/content area? This question is testing your knowledge of security of programming code. In your syllabus, this is under the "Apply and evaluate strategies used by software developers to manage the security of programming code" dot point. Revise 1.9 Security Strategies & Tools, if required.
  2. What are we required to do? Highlight the NESA key verb in red so you don't forget it. We are required to explain two strategies used by software developers to manage security of programming code. This means we need to look at the components/causes of two strategies and link those causes to how they protect the security of programming code.

 There is no stimulus for this question so we will skip step 2.

Step 3. Plan your response quickly in your head.

Blockchain has a lot of different components that allow it to work, so before writing the response, take a few seconds to think through how you are going to order the causes and effects to make your links clear and strong.

  1. We will start with a topic sentence that addresses the question.
  2. Next we should identify the effect we are leading to. In this case it's solid security of programming code.
  3. Then we brainstorm causes for the effect(s) which will be our two strategies. Let's choose code reviews and penetration testing. Our job is to describe how the components of code reviews and penetration testing lead to secure code.

Step 4. Write your response

  • Use the correct structure: Make sure you follow the Explain structure. This involves identifying and linking causes to the effects the question specifies.
    • Start with a topic sentence which addresses the terms of the question.
    • Use text connectives between your points and to link cause/effect. Below, the causes are in dark blue font and the effects are in purple font. When linking between causes and effects, you can use phrases like "which causes", "consequently", "as a result", "which means", or "ensures" which will signify to the marker that you are clearly linking cause and effect. However they are not always necessary. You can use your usual text connectives like "furthermore" and "additionally" to connect new ideas/points.
  • Relate to the Scenario/Question. Never forget the golden rule "relate to the scenario/question". This means you should use terms from the question throughout your response make links back to the ideas/context given in the question. Below, the links back to the question have been highlighted in purple. 
  • Give clear examples. Give examples for extra clarity and to show a detailed, nuanced understanding of a concept. You can also use examples to relate back to the scenario. Below, examples are highlighted in blue. 
  • Know your content. It's important to think about where this question comes from in your syllabus as you read the question, recall what you have learned about that topic and then include as much relevant information as you can to flesh out your answer.

Sample Answer Analysis: There is a range of strategies software developers use to secure their code.

Firstly, there are code reviews, which involve a systematic examination of code by coworkers who can leave comments, as well as a system of automated checks to identify logic errors and security vulnerabilities. These checks, both human and automated, reduce the likelihood of code containing any security issues that could be exploited, thereby ensuring the code's security.

Penetration testing is another powerful strategy that simulates real-world attacks on the program code to identify vulnerabilities that may have been missed during implementation. Issues such as insecure APIs, improper authentication, or other security flaws can be identified and addressed before code is shipped, ensuring the final state remains secure.

Step 5. Check your response is correct

Quickly reread the question and try highlighting your response in your head if you're in an exam or in a word processor if you are practicing. Make sure there is enough purple and blue and also some green and yellow.

  1. We have structured our response appropriately for a explain question. Here we have identified the effect we need to answer the question and we've described all the causes the lead to it.
  2. We've related to the scenario. We've also included terms from the question and examples that enhance the nuance and quality of our descriptions of each point.

Marking Criteria (through the eyes of a marker)

How do I get full marks?

  • Relate to the scenario and give examples. In the marking criteria, to get full marks, you must explain clearly how TWO strategies are used to secure programming code. This means breaking down two strategies to show what about them allows/leads to secure code.
  • Structure your response appropriately. An explain question requires a clear cause and effect structure. This means, after your topic sentence which addresses and frames the question, you need to start describing all the causes which link to your first effect and use text connectives here and there to accentuate the link. This will make it easier for the maker to pay you marks. If you do not have a cause and effect structure and simply provide characteristics and features of blockchain with some relation to voting, you will only get three marks since this is only describing, not explaining. You need the clear explain structure to your response to get full marks.
  • Know your content — You need to be on top of your code security strategies. Revise 1.9 Security Strategies & Tools.

I'm completely stuck. How do I maximise my marks?

  • Don't leave the question blank. If you're totally stuck, there are always some basic things you can do to guarantee at least one or two marks. After this, flag the question so you can come back to it after you finish the rest of the exam, hopefully with fresh ideas to claim a few more marks.
  • In this question, providing some relevant information will get you one mark. This could be as simple as providing one or two of the causes or effects.

Justify

Justify Questions

NESA Definition — Justify

Support an argument or conclusion.

Justify questions require you to provide evidence or an explanation that supports an argument or conclusion. It's sort of like a mini essay where you have a thesis, which is the conclusion you are required to support, and you need to come up with all the evidence in the body of the essay to support that thesis.

Answer Structure

  1. Topic sentence or phrase that addresses the question explicitly and sets up the thesis you are supporting.
  2. Body of your response that provides evidence which supports the argument or conclusion.

Sample Answer

Question Breakdown & Tips and Tricks

Question: Recommend and justify a suitable development approach for the e-commerce mobile application.

Step 1. Read the Question Carefully.

When reading a question, it's important to ask these two questions:

  1. What is the topic/content area? This question is testing your knowledge of development approaches. In your syllabus, this is under the "Explore and apply the most suitable development approach to develop, modify and implement an enterprise system" dot point of Enterprise project. If you've forgotten this, revise 4.7 Development Approach.
  2. What are we required to do? Highlight the NESA key verb in red so you don't forget it. We are required to recommend and justify a suitable development approach for the e-commerce mobile application in the scenario. This means we need to identify a suitable development approach, and then we need to provide evidence for why it is a good pick. Note, this is more of a skills application question since you are not regurgitating information, but rather applying your analysis and justification skills to make and support and judgement based on an unseen scenario. This makes it harder than some of the earlier questions we looked at and may take some extra time.

Stimulus:

A software company has been contracted to develop a mobile application for a new e-commerce business.

The application must be delivered within six months to meet the client’s launch date. It must include key features such as secure user authentication, a shopping cart, and payment gateway integration.

The solution has to have the ability to scale as the business grows. The client doesn't have a large budget, so they would like the keep costs relatively low.

Step 2. Analyse the stimulus.

Since we know we are answering a development approach question, we should recall all the development approaches we know before we read the stimulus. These are waterfall (structured), agile, prototyping, end user, and outsourcing. If you struggle with these questions, write down each of these approaches in the answer text box and then you can delete the ones that will be too hard to justify as you read the stimulus.

In the first line, the general premise of the stimulus have been set. We need to put ourselves in the shoes of a software company, that has been contracted to develop a mobile application for a new e-commerce business. The end user approach is immediately out since the e-commerce business has hired our software agency rather than doing it themselves. Now, mobile applications, especially for e-commerce businesses are generally medium quality products meaning they have to be robust, but not to the same level of rigour as an air traffic system at an airpot. This means that the agile development approach is already a decent option and the traditional waterfall approach is probably harder, but we won't eliminate it yet.

As we keep reading, we see that the product needs to be "delivered within six months", so this makes it even harder to justify the waterfall approach. The next key phrase we see is "key features" which points us further in the direction of agile which focuses of delivering high priority features iteratively to produce a MVP at a relatively fast pace. Right now, agile is looking pretty good, but prototyping and outsourcing are still open (though, harder to justify with the current evidence given their characteristics). However, the next key phrase, "scale as the business grows" makes them both less viable and agile a better option since agile has the flexible to shift and grow iteratively. Finally, the client "doesn't have a large budget" means waterfall is super hard to justify now, and agile has a lot more going for it now.

Based on what we know about each development approach, we can easily recommend Agile, but now we need to produce the evidence that supports that recommendation.

Step 3. Plan your response quickly in your head.

For a recommend and justify question, we just need to have a topic sentence that introduces the item we are recommending and then a body which provides reasons and evidence for why our recommendation stands in relation to the stimulus and question.

Our recommendation will be the Agile approach.

Our evidence will be:

  • Prioritisation of a MVP to quickly deliver a product with key features.
  • Flexibility of agile to accomodate evolving future need.
  • Small, skilled dev team minimises costs for a limited budget.

After each piece of evidence, we need to explicitly link it back to how it supports the agile development approach.

Step 4. Write your response

  • Follow the right structure for a recommend and justify question:
    • Start with a topic sentence which addresses the terms of the question and clearly introduces the thing you are supporting. In this case we are supporting a recommendation for a development approach.
    • Use text connectives between your pieces of evidence to segment them for the marker. Good text connectives are "furthermore", "additionally", and "moreover".
    • After each piece of evidence, we need to explicitly link it back to how it supports the agile development approach.
  • Relate to the Scenario/Question. Never forget the golden rule "relate to the scenario/question". This means you should use terms from the question throughout your response make links back to the ideas/context given in the question. In this case, relating to the scenario, will involve mentioning the e-commerce business and their requirements from the stimulus and how Agile's characteristics are a good fit for their needs. Below, the links back to the question have been highlighted in purple. 
  • Give clear examples. When there is no explicit scenario, it's important to give examples to enhance the clarity and nuance of answer. In this describe question, giving examples is an extremely powerful way to elevate your description and prove to the marker you know what you are talking about.
  • Know your content. It's important to think about where this question comes from in your syllabus as you read the question, recall what you have learned about that topic and then include as much relevant information as you can to flesh out your answer.

Sample Answer Analysis: The Agile development approach is the most suitable for developing the e-commerce mobile application. Agile is centred around iterative development in scrum cycles, allowing for rapid delivery of a minimum viable product (MVP) within the six-month deadline. This ensures that essential features, such as secure authentication and payment integration, can be prioritised and delivered early in the project. Furthermore, the flexibility of Agile also supports future scalability by enabling continuous updates and improvements in response to the business's growth and evolving user needs. Additionally, Agile minimises costs by focusing on high-priority features in each iteration, reducing unnecessary development work.

Step 5. Check your response is correct

Quickly reread the question and try highlighting your response in your head if you're in an exam or in a word processor if you are practicing. Make sure there is enough purple and blue and also some green and yellow.

  1. We have structured our response appropriately for a justify question. Here we have clearly identified the thing we are supporting and provided three strong pieces of evidence to justify the recommendation.
  2. We've related to the scenario. We've also included terms from the question and our pieces of evidence explicitly link to the stimulus and question.

Marking Criteria (through the eyes of a marker)

How do I get full marks?

  • Relate to the scenario and give examples. In the marking criteria, to get full marks, you must justify a suitable development approach with at least two major points in relation to the scenario. Here the scenario is the requirements/constraints of the e-commerce business and we need to provide evidence that supports agile in relation to these requirements which were time frame, small budget, and evolving needs.
  • Structure your response appropriately. A justify question needs to have clear pieces of evidence that support your thesis in the topic sentence. In this case we need to have clear evidence in the body that supports the use of the Agile development approach. When writing your response, it's like a mini essay, you need to convince your reader of something, so use evaluative language, and build the argument up bit by bit as you add more evidence.
  • Know your content — You need to be on top of your development approaches and know how to apply them to a scenario. Revise 4.7 Development Approach.

I'm completely stuck. How do I maximise my marks?

  • Don't leave the question blank. If you're totally stuck, there are always some basic things you can do to guarantee at least one or two marks. After this, flag the question so you can come back to it after you finish the rest of the exam, hopefully with fresh ideas to claim a few more marks.
  • In this question, providing some relevant information will get you one mark. This could be as simple as recommending Agile with some of it's most common features. If you provide a proper description of agile, you can get two marks, and if you justify and link the features of agile to why is suitable for a project in general you will get three marks. To get four marks, you need to choose features of agile that make it desirable for the specific requirements specified in the stimulus which where the time frame, cost, and evolving needs.
  • Try and put yourself in the shoes of the scenario. Imagine you are a software company tasks with creating this e-commerce app. Given the budget and time restrains and the possibility for changing requirements, what development approach would you pitch to the team manager. You need to prove to the team manager why your approach has the best characteristics for the given constraints on the project.

Assess

Assess Questions

NESA Definition — Assess

Make a judgement of value, quality, outcomes, results or size.

These assess questions tend to be worth more marks (5+) and are typically located near the end of your exam. They usually require a mini essay like structure with a short introduction and then paragraphs delving into your points and finally, a summarising conclusion at the end.

Answer Structure

  1. A topic sentence or introduction paragraph that introduces your judgement of value, quality, outcomes, results or size.
  2. The body of your response is usually a few paragraphs that supports the judgement you made in your introduction by exploring different points and how they fit together. Each sentence you write should be form the mindset of evaluating the value, quality, outcome, result or size of something and how this supports your overall judgement in the response.
  3. A conclusion that summarises everything is optional, but a good thing for completeness especially for questions more than 6 marks.

Assess — Example Question (without annotations)

Assess — Example Question (annotated answer with though process)

Sample Answer

Automation has significantly influenced individuals, society, and the environment, offering many benefits and challenges.

For individuals, automation has enhanced worker safety by replacing humans in hazardous tasks. For example, in the mining industry, autonomous haulage systems (AHS) have reduced safety incidents by 50%, removing workers from dangerous environments. However, automation also introduces risks, such as technical malfunctions, which can lead to accidents if safety protocols are not followed or rigorous enough. Moreover, automation provides opportunities for people with disabilities, such as robotic exoskeletons enabling mobility and voice-activated systems increasing independence. Yet, individuals with cognitive disabilities face displacement in routine jobs without retraining programs.

Societally, automation reshapes employment by reducing demand for repetitive tasks while creating opportunities in technical fields. For example, Foxconn replaced 60,000 workers with robots but retrained employees to maintain and oversee these systems. This shift necessitates continuous up-skilling, as traditional roles give way to jobs requiring technical expertise. Without accessible training initiatives, economic disparities may widen, disproportionately affecting low-skilled workers.

Environmentally, automation improves production efficiency and reduces waste. A core example is Tesla’s Gigafactory. By integrating robotics and renewable energy, Tesla minimises material loss and environmental impact and drastically improves overall production efficiency. Similarly, automated agricultural systems reduce water and pesticide waste through precision application using computer vision. However, automation increases energy consumption, particularly in data centres, which accounted for 1% of global electricity use in 2021. Sustainable practices, like investing in green technologies, are essential to mitigate these environmental impacts.

Overall, automation offers substantial benefits in safety, inclusivity, efficiency, and waste reduction. However, challenges such as displacement, skill demands, and environmental concerns must be addressed through targeted policies and investments to ensure equitable and sustainable outcomes.

Question Breakdown & Tips and Tricks

Question: Assess the impact of automation on individuals, society, and the environment. (8 marks)

Step 1. Read the Question Carefully.

When reading a question, it's important to ask these two questions

  1. What is the topic/content area? This question is testing your knowledge of automation, but also the skill of making a judgement on it's impact. Specifically, it's looking for the impact of automation on individuals, society, and the environment. In your syllabus, this is under the "Assess the impact of automation on the individual, society and the environment" dot point of your software automation topic. Revise 3.9 Impact of Automation, if required.
  2. What are we required to do? Highlight the NESA key verb in red so you don't forget it. Assess the impact of automation on individuals, society, and the environment. This means we need to make a judgement on the impact/outcomes which means breaking down the idea of automation into smaller parts that we can assess individually to support over overall judgement. The stimulus guides us on what smaller components to look at — individuals, society, and the environment. It's up to us to assess the components of each of these and make a judgement of the impact automation has had on each of them. This will mean we need a few paragraphs. Since this is an eight mark question, we have about 14 minutes to plan and write a response.

Stimulus:

There was a rather long stimulus provided for this question. This may be formatted as a video or slideshow you are able to scrub/scroll through.

Automation is transforming industries across the globe, from manufacturing to agriculture, with far-reaching effects on individuals, society, and the environment. By integrating advanced technologies such as robotics and artificial intelligence, companies can increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety.

Case Study 1: Worker Safety in Mining
The mining industry has adopted autonomous haulage systems (AHS) to replace human drivers in hazardous conditions. For example, Rio Tinto has implemented AHS in Australian mines, reducing safety incidents by 50%. These systems remove workers from dangerous environments but require new technical skills for remote operation and maintenance.

Case Study 2: Inclusivity for People with Disabilities
Assistive automation technologies are improving access to work for people with disabilities. Robotic exoskeletons enable mobility-impaired individuals to perform tasks previously inaccessible, while AI-powered assistants like Siri enhance workplace productivity. However, automation of routine jobs risks displacing workers with cognitive disabilities, emphasising the need for retraining initiatives.

Case Study 3: Environmental Impacts of Automation
Automation can optimise resource use and reduce waste. Tesla’s Gigafactory uses AI-driven robotics and renewable energy to minimise production costs and environmental impact, while precision agriculture systems reduce water and pesticide waste. However, the energy demands of automated systems, such as data centres, raise concerns about sustainability.

Step 2. Analyse the stimulus.

In longer stimuli like this, the idea is to note down parts of it that will support your idea/argument and any clues it gives about the smaller components you need to assess.

Step 3. Plan your response quickly in your head.

In your head take a mental note of the two things you are required to do which are making a judgement on the effectiveness of data visualisation in the context of enterprise decision making and then supporting this by breaking the topic into smaller components which we assess individually.

Step 4. Write your response

  • Use the correct structure: Make sure you follow the assess structure. This involves making a relevant judgement followed by an explanation/description of the constituent components/ideas that make up the topic and lead to your overall judgement.
  • Relate to the Scenario/Question. This means you should use terms from the question throughout your response, make links back to the ideas/context given in the question, and draw from the stimulus. Below, the links back to the question have been highlighted in purple. 
  • Give clear examples. When there is no explicit scenario, it's important to give examples to enhance the clarity and nuance of answer. In this describe question, giving examples is an extremely powerful way to elevate your description and prove to the marker you know what you are talking about.
  • Know your content. It's important to think about where this question comes from in your syllabus as you read the question, recall what you have learned about that topic and then include as much relevant information as you can to flesh out your answer.

 Sample Answer Analysis: Automation has significantly influenced individuals, society, and the environment, offering many benefits and challenges.

For individuals, automation has enhanced worker safety by replacing humans in hazardous tasks. For example, in the mining industry, autonomous haulage systems (AHS) have reduced safety incidents by 50%, removing workers from dangerous environments. However, automation also introduces risks, such as technical malfunctions, which can lead to accidents if safety protocols are not followed or rigorous enough. Moreover, automation provides opportunities for people with disabilities, such as robotic exoskeletons enabling mobility and voice-activated systems increasing independence. Yet, individuals with cognitive disabilities face displacement in routine jobs without retraining programs.

Societally, automation reshapes employment by reducing demand for repetitive tasks while creating opportunities in technical fields. For example, Foxconn replaced 60,000 workers with robots but retrained employees to maintain and oversee these systems. This shift necessitates continuous up-skilling, as traditional roles give way to jobs requiring technical expertise. Without accessible training initiatives, economic disparities may widen, disproportionately affecting low-skilled workers.

Environmentally, automation improves production efficiency and reduces waste. A core example is Tesla’s Gigafactory. By integrating robotics and renewable energy, Tesla minimises material loss and environmental impact and drastically improves overall production efficiency. Similarly, automated agricultural systems reduce water and pesticide waste through precision application using computer vision. However, automation increases energy consumption, particularly in data centres, which accounted for 1% of global electricity use in 2021. Sustainable practices, like investing in green technologies, are essential to mitigate these environmental impacts.

Overall, automation offers substantial benefits in safety, inclusivity, efficiency, and waste reduction. However, challenges such as displacement, skill demands, and environmental concerns must be addressed through targeted policies and investments to ensure equitable and sustainable outcomes.

Step 5. Check your response is correct

Quickly reread the question and try highlighting your response in your head if you're in an exam or in a word processor if you are practicing. Make sure there is enough purple and blue since relating to the scenario and giving examples is core to getting in the top band, then ensuring there is good content knowledge shining through from your understanding of the course in yellow and a correct structure in red is extremely important too.

We were able to start with a clear judgement, we then explained our assessment that led to the judgement.

 Marking Criteria (through the eyes of a marker)

 

How do I get full marks?

  • Structure your response appropriately. To get full marks you need to have a well-informed and balanced judgement of the impact of automation on each of the three areas specified with relation to the stimulus. To be well informed, you need to have accurate ideas, stats, and information in each paragraph and link it to your judgement on the impact. Having a balanced argument means you need to look at everything, both negative and positive which we did for each point.
  • Relate to the scenario. You need to relate "to the stimulus" by writing about the three area specified and drawing explicitly from the stimulus.
  • Include examples. These allow you to relate to the stimulus better and appear more "well-informed".
  • Know your content — You need to be "well-informed" and on top of your software automation topic. Your response should include key content that fleshes out your response.

I'm completely stuck. How do I maximise my marks?

  • Don't leave the question blank. If you're totally stuck, there are always some basic things you can do to guarantee at least one or two marks. After this, flag the question so you can come back to it after you finish the rest of the exam, hopefully with fresh ideas to claim a few more marks.
  • As per the marking criteria, you can get one mark for providing "some relevant information".  Always put something down even if you don't think it's correct since you won't have marks taken away for doing something wrong, you only gain marks for doing things right.
  • Even if you don't know how to make a proper judgement, simply describing some of the plausible impacts of automation will get you three marks and relating it closer to the scenario by describing how it impacts the three categories will bump you up from there.

Analyse

Analyse Questions

NESA Definition — Analyse

  • Identify components and the relationship between them.
  • Draw out and relate implications.

These assess questions tend to be worth more marks (5+) and are typically located near the end of your exam. They usually require a mini essay like structure with a short introduction and then paragraphs delving into your points and finally, a summarising conclusion at the end.

Answer Structure

  1. A brief introduction/thesis that introduces your understanding of all the components and the implications of them/relationship between them.
  2. A body that explains each of the smaller components, their implications and how the relate.
  3. A conclusion that summarises your ideas and restates the final implication of the analysis.

Analyse — Example Question (without annotations)

Analyse — Example Question (annotated answer with though process)

Sample Answer

The development and implementation of safe and secure software have significant social, ethical, and legal implications for both individuals and enterprises.

There are many social issues. For individuals, secure software protects sensitive data, such as personal and financial information, fostering trust in digital systems. However, increased security measures can inadvertently restrict access to services, particularly for those less technologically such as two-factor authentication and passkeys. For enterprises, secure software reshapes employment opportunities, creating demand for roles like cybersecurity analysts while reducing reliance on traditional IT positions. This workforce transformation requires companies to invest in re-skilling initiatives to support displaced workers, ensuring the benefits of secure software are equitably distributed.

Ethically, secure software development raises challenges regarding privacy, transparency, and responsibility. Individuals benefit from software that protects their data and respects their rights, but they also expect control over how their information is used. Developers and enterprises must balance innovation with user empowerment, implementing features like data anonymisation and encryption. For businesses, there is a moral obligation to safeguard customer data and avoid practices that exploit user information for profit. Ethical dilemmas also arise when companies rely on proprietary systems to maintain market advantage, potentially limiting access to secure software for public benefit.

Legally, secure software development involves navigating complex regulatory landscapes. Individuals are protected by laws such as the GDPR, which grant rights over their data and ensure accountability from organisations. For enterprises, compliance with legal standards is both a necessity and a challenge, as breaches can result in substantial fines and reputational damage. Intellectual property laws further complicate the development process, as companies must protect their innovations while respecting the contributions of others. For example, a company may patent its encryption methods to secure its competitive edge while licensing them for collaborative use.

In conclusion, safe and secure software development has profound social, ethical, and legal ramifications, affecting individuals and enterprises in interconnected ways.

Question Breakdown & Tips and Tricks

Question: Analyse the social, ethical, and legal implications of developing and implementing safe and secure software. (8 marks)

Step 1. Read the Question Carefully.

When reading a question, it's important to ask these two questions

  1. What is the topic/content area? This question is testing your knowledge of social, ethical, and legal issues in developing secure software. Particularly we are looking at these issues and their implications for developing and implement safe and secure software. This is under the "Evaluate the social, ethical and legal issues and ramifications that affect people and enterprises..." dot point of your secure software architecture topic. Revise 1.17 Social/Ethical/Legal Issues, if required.
  2. What are we required to do? Highlight the NESA key verb in red so you don't forget it. We are required to analyse social, ethical and legal implication meaning we need to identify what makes up these issues and relate them together.

Stimulus: As software becomes integral to modern life, ensuring its safety and security has far-reaching implications. Protecting sensitive data, complying with legal standards, and addressing ethical concerns are central to software development. However, these considerations bring challenges. For example, robust security measures enhance data protection but raise costs, potentially excluding smaller businesses. Similarly, while privacy regulations empower users, they can hinder innovation and collaboration. The evolving nature of threats means developers must navigate a complex web of responsibilities to individuals and enterprises while fostering trust and innovation.

Step 2. Analyse the stimulus.

This stimulus contain a bit of a guide as to what to include in our response. This question is a little vague is that is allows you to talk about social, ethical, and legal implications in developing secure software in general. In the stimulus, we can see that there is a "complex web of responsibilities for individuals and enterprises", so adding an extra level of specificity by looking as how the issues impact individuals and enterprises will elevate our response.

 

Step 3. Plan your response quickly in your head.

In your head take a mental note of the two things you are required to do which are providing the characteristics and features of rules and facts. Since rules use facts to deduce meaning, it will be more cohesive to place rules second in the response. We will also include a brief topic sentence which immediately addresses the question. When we start writing we now have a map which will guide us.

Step 4. Write your response

  • Use the correct structure: Make sure you follow the analyse structure. This involves picking apart the components of each of your ideas and discussing them and how they relate.
  • Relate to the Scenario/Question. This means you should use terms from the question throughout your response, make links back to the ideas/context given in the question, and draw from the stimulus. Below, the links back to the question have been highlighted in purple. 
  • Give clear examples. When there is no explicit scenario, it's important to give examples to enhance the clarity and nuance of answer. In this describe question, giving examples is an extremely powerful way to elevate your description and prove to the marker you know what you are talking about.
  • Know your content. It's important to think about where this question comes from in your syllabus as you read the question, recall what you have learned about that topic and then include as much relevant information as you can to flesh out your answer.

  2. We have covered all three main points and added extra specificity of individuals and enterprises.
  3. We summarised our conclusion on the impact at the end.

To get full marks you just need to provide a detailed analysis of the social, ethical, and legal implications of developing and implementing safe and secure software.
